title: Exact condensed induction for a split profinite coset projection
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent site of profinite sets [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $P$, let $\mathcal A_P(A)$ be the category of internal $A$-modules with $A$-linear condensed $P$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $H$ be a closed subgroup of $P$. Give the coset space $X=\{pH:p\in P\}$ its quotient topology, and assume it is profinite and that the projection $q:P\to X$ admits a continuous section $s:X\to P$ with $q s=1_X$.

For a profinite test set $S$, write $P_S=C(S,P)$ and $H_S=C(S,H)$. The group algebra $A(S)[P_S]$ consists of finite formal sums $\sum a_p[p]$, with $[p][p']=[pp']$. For $M\in\mathcal A_H(A)$, form the presheaf of $A$-modules
$$S\longmapsto A(S)[P_S]\otimes_{A(S)[H_S]}M(S),$$
with restrictions induced by those of $A,M$ and precomposition of continuous maps. Let $\operatorname{Ind}_H^P M$ be its module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Left multiplication on $P_S$ induces a condensed $P$-action on this sheafification. This construction is an additive exact functor $\operatorname{Ind}_H^P:\mathcal A_H(A)\to\mathcal A_P(A)$, where exact means preservation of short exact sequences of internal equivariant modules. It is left adjoint to restriction $\operatorname{Res}_H^P$. The adjunction sends $F:\operatorname{Ind}_H^P M\to N$ to $m\mapsto F([1]\otimes m)$; its inverse sends an $H$-equivariant map $f:M\to\operatorname{Res}_H^P N$ to $[p]\otimes m\mapsto p\cdot f(m)$ and then factors through sheafification. No finiteness assumption on $X$ and no discreteness assumption on $M$ is made.

proof.text: Use the section-module interpretation of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. The subgroup $H$ is profinite: it is closed in the compact Hausdorff group $P$, and its subspace topology has the inherited clopen basis. For $J=H,P$ apply [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] on the specified small profinite site with $K(S)=C(S,J)$ and ring sheaf $A$. This site has finite limits and the given finite jointly surjective covers; $K$ is the condensed group of $J$ and acts trivially on $A$. The cited statement gives equivariant sheafification and says that forgetting the action creates kernels and cokernels, with sectionwise kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels. It also detects zero objects. The categories are abelian by [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation], taking its first group to be $J$ and its second group trivial. Thus exactness can be checked on underlying module sheaves: the image is the kernel of the cokernel, so both image and kernel are created by forgetting, and equality is reflected by the faithful forgetful functor.

proof.text: Write $B_M(S)=A(S)[P_S]\otimes_{A(S)[H_S]}M(S)$. Its elements are finite sums of symbols $a[p]\otimes m$, modulo additivity and the balancing relations $[ph]\otimes m=[p]\otimes h m$ and $a[p]\otimes m=[p]\otimes am$. Restriction along $t:T\to S$ sends such a symbol to $t^*a[p\circ t]\otimes t^*m$; naturality and linearity of the $H$-action preserve both relations. Left multiplication $g([p]\otimes m)=[gp]\otimes m$ also preserves them, is $A(S)$-linear, and is natural in $S$. Its unit and associativity laws follow from $1p=p$ and $g(g'p)=(gg')p$. The equivariant sheafification assertion of [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], together with [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], therefore makes $B_M^\#$ the claimed internal $P$-module. A morphism $u:M\to M'$ acts by $[p]\otimes m\mapsto[p]\otimes u(m)$ before sheafification. Identity, composition, zero and sums of maps have these same formulas; the sheafified maps retain them by uniqueness of their extensions. Hence this is an additive functor $L=\operatorname{Ind}_H^P$.

proof.text: Let $\eta_M:B_M\to L M$ be the sheafification unit. For a $P$-equivariant linear map $F:L M\to N$ define $\Phi(F)_S(m)=F_S(\eta_M([1]\otimes m))$. These maps are linear and commute with restriction. For $h\in H_S$, balancing gives $[1]\otimes hm=[h]\otimes m=h([1]\otimes m)$, so $\Phi(F)(hm)=h\Phi(F)(m)$. Thus $\Phi(F)$ is a morphism $M\to\operatorname{Res}_H^P N$, with precisely the forward formula in the statement.

proof.text: Conversely let $f:M\to\operatorname{Res}_H^P N$ be equivariant. On $B_M(S)$ define $\widetilde f([p]\otimes m)=p f(m)$ and extend linearly to finite sums. It respects balancing since $(ph)f(m)=p f(hm)$, and it respects scalar balancing since every $p$ acts $A(S)$-linearly. These maps commute with restriction, and $\widetilde f(g([p]\otimes m))=gp f(m)=g\widetilde f([p]\otimes m)$. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] there is a unique linear extension $\Psi(f):L M\to N$. It is $P$-equivariant: under the equivalence of [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], $\widetilde f$ is a module-presheaf map on the action site $C_K$, and its extension by the module-sheafification universal property on $C_K$ corresponds to an equivariant map whose underlying extension on the base site is the same unique linear extension. This uses the cited statement's identification of the two sheafifications, including their units.

proof.text: We have $\Phi\Psi(f)(m)=1f(m)=f(m)$. On every presheaf generator, $\Psi\Phi(F)(\eta_M([p]\otimes m))=pF(\eta_M([1]\otimes m))=F(\eta_M([p]\otimes m))$. The universal property in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] makes the resulting sheaf maps equal. For a source map $u:M'\to M$ and a target map $v:N\to N'$, the formula gives $\Phi(vFu)(m)=v\Phi(F)(u(m))$, where on the left $u$ denotes $L u$. This proves naturality of the inverse bijections, hence the asserted adjunction $L\dashv\operatorname{Res}_H^P$ with both specified formulas. No property of $s$ was used for the adjunction.

proof.text: Now use the continuous section to prove preservation of kernels. Put $X_S=C(S,X)$. Every $p\in P_S$ has a unique expression $p=(s\circ x)h$ with $x\in X_S$ and $h\in H_S$: necessarily $x=q\circ p$ and $h=(s\circ q\circ p)^{-1}p$. The latter map has image in $H$ because $p$ and $s(q(p))$ belong to the same right coset. It is continuous as a map to $H$ with its subspace topology, since its composite to $P$ is continuous. Conversely $(x,h)$ has product $(s\circ x)h$ with coset $x$, and these two formulas are inverse. They commute with precomposition by every map of profinite test sets. No normality or finite index of $H$ is used.

proof.text:
Define $D_M(S)=\bigoplus_{x\in X_S}M(S)$, whose elements have finite support, and write $e_x(m)$ for an element supported at $x$. The maps
$$\alpha_S:B_M(S)\longrightarrow D_M(S),\qquad [p]\otimes m\longmapsto e_{qp}\bigl(((s\circ qp)^{-1}p)m\bigr),$$
$$\beta_S:D_M(S)\longrightarrow B_M(S),\qquad e_x(m)\longmapsto[s\circ x]\otimes m$$
are inverse $A(S)$-linear maps. Indeed the factorization of $ph$ is $(x,h_p h)$ if that of $p$ is $(x,h_p)$, so $\alpha_S([ph]\otimes m)=e_x(h_p h m)=\alpha_S([p]\otimes hm)$; scalar balancing follows from linearity of the $H_S$-action. This verifies that $\alpha_S$ is defined on the tensor product. The map $\beta_S$ is linear on each summand, so defines a linear map on finite-support sums. The two composites on generators are
$$e_x(m)\longmapsto e_x(m),\qquad [p]\otimes m\longmapsto[s\circ qp]\otimes h_p m=[p]\otimes m.$$
Additivity then proves both identities on all elements.

proof.text: Give $D_M$ restriction maps $e_x(m)\mapsto e_{x\circ t}(t^*m)$ along $t:T\to S$, adding coefficients when distinct indices become equal after restriction. The factorization in step 6 shows that $\alpha,\beta$ commute with these restrictions, even when indices merge. They are also natural in equivariant maps $M\to M'$, since such a map commutes with every $h_p$. Thus $B_M\cong D_M$ as module presheaves, naturally in $M$. This assertion concerns finite-support sums indexed by continuous maps $S\to X$; it does not identify them with a product, nor with a sum indexed by individual points of $X$.

proof.text: For an equivariant map $u:M\to N$, let $K=\ker u$. By [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], $K(S)=\ker u_S$. Under the normal forms of steps 7--8, $B_u(S)$ applies $u_S$ to each coefficient, so its kernel consists exactly of finite-support sums with coefficients in $K(S)$. The inclusion $B_K(S)\to B_M(S)$ is injective and identifies $B_K$ with the presheaf kernel of $B_u$, naturally in $S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] to the ringed profinite site $(C,A)$. It preserves this kernel, so the underlying module sheaf of $L K$ is the kernel of the underlying map $L u$. The comparison is $P$-equivariant by construction in step 2; the action-site kernel assertion identifies it with the equivariant kernel as well. Consequently $L$ preserves kernels. This uses exact sheafification only for a sectionwise kernel diagram, and does not assume that epimorphisms of condensed modules are surjective on sections.

proof.text: Let $u:M'\to M$ and let $v:M\to Q$ be its cokernel in the abelian action category of step 1. A map $a:L M\to N$ with $aL u=0$ corresponds by the natural adjunction of step 5 to a map $b:M\to\operatorname{Res}N$ with $bu=0$. There is a unique $c:Q\to\operatorname{Res}N$ with $cv=b$; its adjoint $d:L Q\to N$ is the unique map with $dL v=a$, by the same naturality. Also $L v L u=L(vu)=0$ by additivity. This is the cokernel universal property, so $L$ preserves cokernels. Finally, in a short exact sequence $0\to M'\xrightarrow{u}M\xrightarrow{v}M''\to0$, $u$ is the kernel of $v$ and $v$ is the cokernel of $u$. Steps 9 and 10 preserve both descriptions, which proves that the induced sequence is short exact. All finite-support formulas allow arbitrary $X_S$ and arbitrary section modules, establishing the last clause as well.
